candidates.review_note: The task asks only which coin is counterfeit, not whether it is heavy or light. For k weighings without an initially known genuine coin, the capacity is (3^k-1)/2; the all-balanced branch may leave one coin with both possible signs. A first weighing of equal groups reduces an imbalance to signed candidates and supplies genuine coins outside those groups; a balance supplies known genuine coins on the pans. This yields the ternary capacity recurrence and achievable bound for every n>=3. With exactly two coins, swapping which coin is counterfeit and reversing its sign leaves every possible comparison unchanged, so identification is impossible regardless of k.
